findings.issue_text: **C1. `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` silently no-ops membership changes and flips the group invisible** — `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34-47`
**C2. `create` silently discards `alias_level`, which the form now collects** — `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-32`, with `models/group.js:62-68` and `admin/templates/group.hbs:41-44`
**I1. `remove_member` raises `RecordNotFound` when the user isn't in the group** — `admin/groups_controller.rb:90`

`group.users.delete(user_id)` — `CollectionAssociation#delete` resolves integer args via `records = find(records)`, **scoped to the association**, so a non-member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` → 404, not the `success_json` below it. Admin double-clicks the remove "×": first succeeds, second 404s. `Discourse.Group#removeMember` (`models/group.js:40-49`) has **no rejection handler**, so `findMembers()` never runs, the list never refreshes, and the admin sees nothing. The deleted spec `it "succeeds silently when removing non-members"` documented the old contract; the behavior changed with nothing replacing it. Fix: resolve the user explicitly and make removal idempotent; add a `.catch` client-side.
**I2. `group.users.delete(...)` bypasses `Group#remove` and join-model callbacks [unverified]** — `admin/groups_controller.rb:90`

Related (same file `:29-48`, `models/group.js:23`): clamping offset to `user_count` rather than to the last page boundary can land `offset` on a non-multiple of `limit`, after which `currentPage = floor(offset/limit)+1` no longer describes the visible window. Clamp to `(totalPages - 1) * limit`. **There is no test of any kind for `currentPage`/`totalPages`/`next`/`previous`** — this is the PR's new logic and a three-line unit test would have caught the bug.
**I4. `/groups/:name/members.json` accepts unbounded `limit` and negative `offset`** — `groups_controller.rb:22-26`
**I7. Member fetching moved from `afterModel` to `setupController` — loses loading substate and all error handling** — `admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:11-14`, `routes/group-members.js.es6:8-12`
**I9. `add_members`/`remove_member` error handling is structurally dead code; bad usernames vanish silently** — `admin/groups_controller.rb:65-97`
**I10. Adding an already-present member is unhandled [unverified]** — `admin/groups_controller.rb:71-75`
**I11. Breaking response-shape change to public `/groups/:name/members.json`** — `groups_controller.rb:28-35`

**M1** `spec/.../groups_controller_spec.rb:52,94,115` — hard-coded seeded `id: 1` (i.e. `Group::AUTO_GROUPS[:admins]`) couples three specs to seed ordering; `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` is already used at `:65`.

**M2** `spec:115` — `xhr :put, :remove_member` uses the wrong verb; the only route is `delete "members"` (`config/routes.rb:49`). Passes only because controller specs generate URLs without considering the verb. `:125` gets it right.
**M3** `groups_controller.rb:25` — `total = group.users.count` is a second query per request when `groups.user_count` already exists; only worth switching after I2 is resolved.
**M4** `admin_base.scss:462-481` — literal `#333`/`#aaa` instead of `$primary`/`scale-color(...)` breaks dark schemes, and four `!important`s suggest a specificity fight better fixed by scoping.
**M5** `admin_base.scss:164` and `:461` — `.groups` styles split across two blocks ~300 lines apart.

**M6** `admin-group-selector.hbs`, `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs` — pure whitespace churn, unrelated to the fix. The latter adds whitespace *inside* `<a>` elements, which can change inline spacing in the autocomplete dropdown (probably harmless, worth an eyeball).

**M7** `group.hbs:16-18` — the `disabled` class on pagination links is cosmetic; the action still fires (correctly guarded in the controller, so defense-in-depth only). `pointer-events: none` would make the affordance honest.
**M8** `models/group.js:10-12` — `limit`/`offset`/`user_count` get defaults but `members` doesn't; add `members: null` for consistency.
**M9** `models/group.js:70` — instance method `create` now sits alongside `Discourse.Group.create` (the class factory, used at `:35`, `:104`, `:116`). Works, but a readability trap.

**M10** `admin/groups_controller.rb:101-103` — automatic-group rejection changed 403 (`Discourse::InvalidAccess`) → 422. Consistent with `destroy`, so probably right, but another undocumented client-visible change.
**M11** `group.hbs:28` — `id="group-users"` → `id="user-selector"`; `grep -r "group-users"` against the full tree before merging.
**M12** `admin/groups_controller.rb:99-103`, `groups_controller.rb:38-45` — methods indented under `protected`/`private`, differing from surrounding convention; may trip a linter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **C1. `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` silently no-ops membership changes and flips the group invisible** — `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34-47`

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the old `request.patch?` branch that handled membership changes via `params[:changes]` was removed. Now any PATCH to `/admin/groups/:id` will run the same code path as PUT, which ignores `params[:changes]` (so membership changes no-op). Worse, it unconditionally does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`; when `visible` is omitted (typical for a membership-only PATCH), this evaluates to `false`, flipping the group to invisible and saving it. This regression is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **C2. `create` silently discards `alias_level`, which the form now collects** — `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-32`, with `models/group.js:62-68` and `admin/templates/group.hbs:41-44`

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. The client form always includes the alias level selector (admin/templates/group.hbs shows the combo-box bound to alias_level outside the {{#if id}} block), and the JS model’s asJSON() includes alias_level (discourse/models/group.js). When creating a new group, admin-group.js calls group.create(), which POSTs this.asJSON() directly. However, Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible and never reads params[:alias_level], so any non-default alias_level chosen in the form is ignored on create (but update does handle alias_level).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **I1. `remove_member` raises `RecordNotFound` when the user isn't in the group** — `admin/groups_controller.rb:90`

`group.users.delete(user_id)` — `CollectionAssociation#delete` resolves integer args via `records = find(records)`, **scoped to the association**, so a non-member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` → 404, not the `success_json` below it. Admin double-clicks the remove "×": first succeeds, second 404s. `Discourse.Group#removeMember` (`models/group.js:40-49`) has **no rejection handler**, so `findMembers()` never runs, the list never refreshes, and the admin sees nothing. The deleted spec `it "succeeds silently when removing non-members"` documented the old contract; the behavior changed with nothing replacing it. Fix: resolve the user explicitly and make removal idempotent; add a `.catch` client-side.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes member removal to `group.users.delete(user_id)` in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`. In Rails, `CollectionAssociation#delete` given an Integer typically resolves ids via an association-scoped lookup (effectively `group.users.find(user_id)`), which will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if the user is not currently a member. That exception would prevent the controller from reaching the `render json: success_json` path (and would surface as a 404/500 depending on global rescue behavior). This makes the endpoint non-idempotent (e.g., a double-click remove or retry can fail). On the client side, `Discourse.Group#removeMember` only attaches a `.then(...)` to refresh via `findMembers()` and has no rejection handler, so on error the UI won’t refresh and the admin gets no corrective update. The previous spec coverage for “succeeds silently when removing non-members” was removed with no replacement, consistent with an unintended contract change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **I2. `group.users.delete(...)` bypasses `Group#remove` and join-model callbacks [unverified]** — `admin/groups_controller.rb:90`

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, membership removal is done via `group.users.delete(user_id)` rather than the previously used `group.remove(user)` (seen in the removed `update_patch` logic). This is a concrete behavioral change: it no longer invokes any custom logic encapsulated in `Group#remove`. Additionally, in Rails, `association.delete(...)` typically removes the join row directly (often via `DELETE`/`delete_all`) and does not run callbacks on the join model the way a `destroy`-based path would, so this can bypass join-model callbacks/side effects. That makes the finding a real, verifiable concern introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Related (same file `:29-48`, `models/group.js:23`): clamping offset to `user_count` rather than to the last page boundary can land `offset` on a non-multiple of `limit`, after which `currentPage = floor(offset/limit)+1` no longer describes the visible window. Clamp to `(totalPages - 1) * limit`. **There is no test of any kind for `currentPage`/`totalPages`/`next`/`previous`** — this is the PR's new logic and a three-line unit test would have caught the bug.
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same pagination bug: clamping the next offset to `user_count`/total can produce an invalid offset (e.g., equal to total or not aligned to `limit`), which can yield an empty/incorrect last page and confusing UX. The candidate additionally notes page-number inconsistency and missing tests, but the core issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **I4. `/groups/:name/members.json` accepts unbounded `limit` and negative `offset`** — `groups_controller.rb:22-26`

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then uses them directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. This allows a client to pass an arbitrarily large `limit` (potentially causing heavy queries/large responses) and a negative `offset` (e.g., `-10`), which Rails/DB adapters may reject or behave unexpectedly. The finding accurately describes this newly introduced lack of bounds checking in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **I7. Member fetching moved from `afterModel` to `setupController` — loses loading substate and all error handling** — `admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:11-14`, `routes/group-members.js.es6:8-12`
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that `findMembers()` became asynchronous and is no longer properly handled/awaited, so the controller may render without member data (race condition). The candidate flags that member fetching was moved into `setupController`, which removes the prior route-level loading/error handling and implies the async work is no longer coordinated with the transition. This is effectively the same underlying problem: async member loading is not handled in the route lifecycle, risking missing data and lacking proper substates/error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **I9. `add_members`/`remove_member` error handling is structurally dead code; bad usernames vanish silently** — `admin/groups_controller.rb:65-97`

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split and each is looked up with `User.find_by_username`; missing users are simply skipped (`if user = ...`). So “bad usernames vanish silently” is accurate as behavior. However, that behavior existed previously (the removed specs explicitly asserted silent success when adding non-existent users), so it’s not a newly introduced defect. Also, the claim that the `render_json_error` branches are “structurally dead code” isn’t verifiable from the diff: `group.save` can still fail in principle due to validations/callbacks, so it’s not provably unreachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **I10. Adding an already-present member is unhandled [unverified]** — `admin/groups_controller.rb:71-75`

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code loops over `usernames.split(",")` and calls `group.add(user)` without an explicit membership-exists check. However, the diff does not show the implementation of `Group#add` or the group-membership association constraints, so it’s not verifiable from this change whether adding an already-present user is actually a problem (it may be idempotent, or protected by a uniqueness constraint). The finding is therefore speculative rather than a clearly demonstrated defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **I11. Breaking response-shape change to public `/groups/:name/members.json`** — `groups_controller.rb:28-35`

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the response changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which produces a plain serialized collection/array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e., an object with `members` and `meta` keys. That is a concrete response-shape change for the non-admin `/groups/:name/members(.json)` endpoint and will break any existing consumers expecting the previous top-level array shape (even though the Ember client in this diff was updated to match).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M1** `spec/.../groups_controller_spec.rb:52,94,115` — hard-coded seeded `id: 1` (i.e. `Group::AUTO_GROUPS[:admins]`) couples three specs to seed ordering; `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` is already used at `:65`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple specs hard-coding `id: 1` / `group_id: 1` to exercise “automatic group” behavior (e.g., `xhr :put, :update, id: 1...` and `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1...`; the new `remove_member` context also targets `group_id: 1`). None of these examples create or look up the specific group under test; they implicitly rely on a seeded automatic group having primary key 1. That couples the specs to seed/fixture ordering and can make them brittle if IDs differ, whereas other specs in the same file correctly fabricate an automatic group explicitly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M2** `spec:115` — `xhr :put, :remove_member` uses the wrong verb; the only route is `delete "members"` (`config/routes.rb:49`). Passes only because controller specs generate URLs without considering the verb. `:125` gets it right.
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that the controller spec uses `xhr :put, :remove_member` while the route is defined with `delete "members" => 'groups#remove_member'`, i.e., the test uses the wrong HTTP verb compared to the routing requirement—exactly the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M3** `groups_controller.rb:25` — `total = group.users.count` is a second query per request when `groups.user_count` already exists; only worth switching after I2 is resolved.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce an additional DB query in `GroupsController#members` by doing `total = group.users.count` and then fetching the paginated `members` relation. However, the finding’s core claim that this is unnecessary because an existing `groups.user_count` can be used instead is not verifiable from the diff: the controller does not have `user_count` available without computing it, and whether `Group#user_count` is a counter-cache (cheap) or derived (still a query) is outside what’s shown. Also, the new API response explicitly needs `meta.total` for pagination, so the count query is an intentional tradeoff rather than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M4** `admin_base.scss:462-481` — literal `#333`/`#aaa` instead of `$primary`/`scale-color(...)` breaks dark schemes, and four `!important`s suggest a specificity fight better fixed by scoping.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce hard-coded colors (#333/#aaa) and several `!important` rules in the new `.groups .next, .previous` styles, but the claim that this "breaks dark schemes" is not verifiable from the diff alone (no theming/dark-mode variables or constraints are shown, and use of `$primary`/`scale-color(...)` is an opinionated refactor suggestion). This is primarily a styling/theming preference/specificity concern rather than a clear defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M5** `admin_base.scss:164` and `:461` — `.groups` styles split across two blocks ~300 lines apart.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce two separate `.groups`-related style blocks: one combined selector `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal ... }` near the top of the file, and a later dedicated `.groups { ... }` block for group-specific UI. While the finding is factually accurate (the styles are split), this is a maintainability/style organization nit rather than a verifiable defect, bug, or correctness/security problem introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M6** `admin-group-selector.hbs`, `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs` — pure whitespace churn, unrelated to the fix. The latter adds whitespace *inside* `<a>` elements, which can change inline spacing in the autocomplete dropdown (probably harmless, worth an eyeball).

adjudication.rationale: The changes in `admin-group-selector.hbs` are purely removal of blank lines and have no functional impact. In `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs`, the diff only re-indents HTML and adds line breaks/indentation inside `<a>` elements. While HTML whitespace can sometimes introduce text nodes, this is speculative and not a clear, verifiable defect from the diff alone (and the prior version already had newlines/indentation between inline elements). Overall this is whitespace/style churn rather than a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M7** `group.hbs:16-18` — the `disabled` class on pagination links is cosmetic; the action still fires (correctly guarded in the controller, so defense-in-depth only). `pointer-events: none` would make the affordance honest.

adjudication.rationale: In group.hbs the pagination controls are `<a>` tags whose `class` toggles `disabled` via `showingFirst/showingLast`, but the `{{action "previous"}}`/`{{action "next"}}` handlers still exist. However, in the controller both actions explicitly guard (`if (this.get("showingLast")) { return; }` and similarly for `showingFirst`), so clicking a "disabled" link causes no state change and no request. Also the `<a>` tags have no `href`, so there’s no default navigation to suppress. This is at most a UX/accessibility enhancement suggestion (making the affordance non-clickable), not a verifiable bug/defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M8** `models/group.js:10-12` — `limit`/`offset`/`user_count` get defaults but `members` doesn't; add `members: null` for consistency.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group` sets defaults for `limit`, `offset`, and `user_count`, but omitting an initial `members` property is not a verifiable defect. `members` is populated via `setProperties` inside `findMembers()`, and Ember can handle properties being undefined until set. The templates/routes call `model.findMembers()` and iterate `{{each ... in members}}`; an undefined `members` is typically treated as empty (no crash shown in diff). The proposed change is a consistency/style preference, not a real bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M9** `models/group.js:70` — instance method `create` now sits alongside `Discourse.Group.create` (the class factory, used at `:35`, `:104`, `:116`). Works, but a readability trap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an *instance* method `create` on `Discourse.Group` and updates callers to use `group.create()` (instance) vs `Discourse.Group.create(...)` (class factory). This does not introduce a correctness/security defect in the shown code: Ember/Discourse class factories remain available on the constructor, and the instance method name doesn’t collide at runtime with the class method. The proposed issue is primarily a readability/maintenance concern (“trap”), i.e., a style/naming nit, not a verifiable bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M10** `admin/groups_controller.rb:101-103` — automatic-group rejection changed 403 (`Discourse::InvalidAccess`) → 422. Consistent with `destroy`, so probably right, but another undocumented client-visible change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the rejection behavior for automatic groups in the new membership endpoints: `add_members`/`remove_member` now call `can_not_modify_automatic`, which renders a 422. Previously, automatic-group membership changes in `update_patch` raised `Discourse::InvalidAccess`, which the spec expected to yield 403. However, the old PATCH-based membership API was removed entirely and replaced with these new endpoints, and the specs were updated/added to explicitly expect 422 for these cases. This is an intentional API/status-code change shown in the diff, not a clear bug or defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M11** `group.hbs:28` — `id="group-users"` → `id="user-selector"`; `grep -r "group-users"` against the full tree before merging.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the `user-selector` element’s `id` in `group.hbs` (old `id="group-users"` removed, new `id="user-selector"` added). However, the proposed finding only suggests grepping for remaining references to `group-users` elsewhere in the tree; the diff itself does not show any code still referencing `group-users` that would now break. Without an in-diff reference (JS selector, CSS, test, etc.) relying on the old ID, this is speculative and not a verifiable defect introduced by the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **M12** `admin/groups_controller.rb:99-103`, `groups_controller.rb:38-45` — methods indented under `protected`/`private`, differing from surrounding convention; may trip a linter.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `can_not_modify_automatic` in `Admin::GroupsController` and `find_group` in `GroupsController` are indented under `protected`/`private` (extra spaces before `def`). This does not change Ruby semantics and is not a correctness/security defect introduced by the change; at most it’s a formatting/style convention issue that might affect a linter configuration, which is speculative and not a verifiable problem in the diff itself.
